id: South Sydney Rabbitohs v One New Zealand Warriors-Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: South Sydney Rabbitohs v One New Zealand Warriors
long_description:
The South Sydney Rabbitohs make the trip to Wellington to take on the One New Zealand Warriors in an explosive pre-season clash this February. 

The Bunnies, as they’re affectionately known by their fans, are one of the NRL’s most historic clubs. Since forming in 1908, they’re the most successful NRL club of all time. They’ve won 21 premiership titles and are led by their legendary ‘super coach’ Wayne Bennett. 

It’s the Warriors’ first return to Wellington since the sold-out ANZAC match at Hnry Stadium in 2026. They edged the Redcliffe Dolphins 20 to 18 that night. They’ll be looking for another strong performance to get their 2027 campaign started on the right foot. 

With two of last season’s top six teams squaring off in a summer afternoon kick-off, the stage is set for an electrifying celebration of rugby league.

id: My Fair Lady-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: My Fair Lady
venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Experience the wit, romance, and timeless music of Lerner and Loewe. Written in the 1950s, the musical ‘My Fair Lady’ continues to prove popular with audiences today. This spectacular production brings together some of New Zealand’s leading musical theatre talent, backed by Orchestra Wellington. 

Based on George Bernard Shaw’s ‘Pygmalion’, the story follows spirited flower seller Eliza Doolittle as she crosses paths with the formidable linguistic expert Professor Henry Higgins. Their encounter sets off a journey that’s as heartwarming as it is hilarious. The show includes beloved songs such as Wouldn’t It Be Loverly, The Rain in Spain, and I Could Have Danced All Night. 

Presented by the team that’s brought local smash hits Matilda, Mamma Mia, and Wicked (Capital Theatre Trust and G&T Productions) this loverly production promises to have you dancing all night.

id: Drum Tao-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Drum Tao
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
The rhythm is going to get you when you experience the tremendous appeal of Japan’s Drum Tao. After captivating more than 10 million people worldwide, the breathtaking drumming production returns to New Zealand. It fuses the power of taiko drumming with martial arts athleticism, choreography, and cinematic staging. Drum Tao transcends borders and redefines live performance. This is not just a concert — it delivers artistry, intensity, and passion that will leave you exhilarated and inspired.

With its spectacle, energy, and universal appeal, Drum Tao is a thrilling experience for audiences of all ages.

id: Dragon-Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall-Wellington NZ
name: Dragon
venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
long_description:
Legendary rock band Dragon is celebrating more than five decades of music-making with a tour that visits Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall. The focus of the concert is their hit April Sun in Cuba. It has become the soundtrack for multiple Kiwi generations and remains one of the most instantly recognisable anthems in New Zealand music history. The band formed in Ponsonby in 1972 and five years later it’s fourth studio album, Running Free, spawned the iconic song. It launched Dragon into the mainstream on both sides of the Tasman. April Sun in Cuba has since earned a 5x Platinum certification in Aotearoa and is a fixture of radio, road trips, parties and live shows.

You’ll hear plenty of other songs as well including enduring hits like Rain, Still in Love with You, and Young Years. These are songs that have stood the test of time and continue to connect with audiences across generations.

Joining Dragon on stage is another New Zealand band with a huge reputation. Wellington’s own Fur Patrol will play from its catalogue of three albums. Anyone who has caught the band in recent years will attest that they have lost none of their potency, power, or energy.

id: Welly Wonderland-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Welly Wonderland
venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
You can’t deny it — the Christmas bells are ringing out. This year celebrate the festive season with some of the region’s cherished music groups. Wellington Brass Band join forces with Pacific Connection and St Mark’s Children’s Choir. Together they will transform the Michael Fowler Centre into a magical Christmasy world. Hear your favourite carols in a concert is designed to get you in the mood for Christmas. 

Pacific Connection was formed in 2019 with the goal of providing a space for Pacific people within the local area to sing and perform. Often using barbershop singing style, it uses music to connect generations, communities, and traditions. Wellington Brass Band is Aotearoa’s leading brass ensemble. Together, they’ll bring the Wellington community an afternoon packed with Christmas bangers and big brass moments.

id: Bron Lewis: Brutal-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Bron Lewis: Brutal
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Life is getting brutal for Bron Lewis. Her house is chaotic, her kids are growing in size and sass, and every social interaction feels increasingly gruelling. She might have to bite her tongue in everyday life, but on stage, nothing is held back. 

Following sold-out national and international tours, the Australian comedian is bringing her brand-new show, Brutal, to Wellington’s Opera House. Expect sharp observations, relatable chaos, and the kind of honesty you may be thinking but wouldn’t dare say aloud.

Since leaving teaching for comedy in 2020, Bron Lewis has quickly risen through Australia’s comedy scene. Her show Probably was nominated for Best Newcomer at the 2023 Melbourne International Comedy Festival, while her 2026 show Chaos received the inaugural VicScreen Greenlight Award. She has also appeared on Guy Montgomery’s Guy Mont Spelling Bee, Thank God You’re Here and Have You Been Paying Attention?

See just how brutal she can be when Bron Lewis takes the stage in Wellington.
